title: How to Create a Cross-Chain ERC-20 Token with CCTP | Circle
summary: Learn why crosschain token identity matters, how CCTP burn-and-mint works, and how to connect non-USDC ERC-20s - including a native path on Arc Testnet.
body_markdown:
Applications settle, post collateral, and show balances on a specific chain. If your ERC-20 only exists where you minted it, every other venue needs a one-off bridge, a wrapped copy, or a manual ops process. Interoperability means the same economic asset can move to the chain where the application actually runs, under one bridge identity integrators can rely on.


Arc is built for applications that move value, with[fees in USDC](https://www.arc.io/blog/how-gas-works-on-arc) and[deterministic finality](https://www.arc.io/blog/deterministic-finality-on-arc) that keeps CCTP attestation timing predictable. Issue or hold inventory there, then move the same economic asset when settlement, collateral, or rebalancing needs another supported EVM chain.


[CCTP (Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol)](https://www.circle.com/cross-chain-transfer-protocol) is Circle’s crosschain trust layer for that movement. For USDC, the familiar path is burn on the source chain and mint of native USDC on the destination. The same message and attestation infrastructure now supports other ERC-20s.


For issuer-operated tokens you have two options: deploy a native` CrossChainToken` through the service, or configure an ERC-20 you already control as a custom CCTP connection. Both reuse Circle’s message and attestation layer and both use the same transfer call shape.


### How CCTP burn-and-mint works


CCTP moves value by burning on the source and minting on the destination against an attested message.


1. Source burns and emits a message.
2. Iris attests the message.
3. Destination mints when` MessageTransmitterV2` receives the message and attestation, and you submit` receiveMessage` , or Iris` FORWARD` does it when you include that in the fee quote.


For non-USDC assets, that path runs through` CrossChainTokenService` and a per-token manager, not` depositForBurn` on` TokenMessengerV2` .


### Native vs. custom CCTP tokens on Arc


Both paths assume you issue or operate the token (RWA, issuer stable, similar). For tokens that you do not operate, there is also a path for ownerless configuration, but it does not use burn-and-mint. You can refer to the developer documentation for[ownerless vs custom](https://developers.circle.com/cctp/expanded-assets/concepts/ownerless-vs-custom-tokens) to learn more.


Path When How


Native New token designed for CCTP from day one` deployCrossChainToken` on Arc creates` CrossChainToken` + per-token manager; extend with the same deployer + salt


Custom Existing ERC-20 you operate (or you deploy your own ERC-20 first, then connect it) Deploy or bring the token on Arc, then` registerCustomToken` / configure on every chain in the route


**Custom configuration (issuer-operated).** For an ERC-20 you issue or operate (RWA, issuer stable, similar), configure it on every chain in the route with burn-and-mint (` BURN_MINT` ). You set the owner, operator, pauser, rate limits, and max transfer. Circle cannot assume control.


**Native.** The service deploys the ERC-20 and manager for you (` CREATE3` ). Shared` tokenId` comes from deployer wallet + salt. Transfers are burn-and-mint. You still set rate limit and max transfer (at deploy in` tokenManagerSettings` , or later on the manager).


After the token is live on source and destination, both services must trust each other (` isTrustedDomain` ). Then:


1. ` resolveTokenManager(tokenId)`
2. Approve that manager (not the service)
3. Iris quote — check` feeTotalAmount`
4. ` crossChainTransfer` on` CrossChainTokenService` (fee in source native; recipient gets the full amount)
5. Destination` receiveMessage` , or` FORWARD` in the quote


Decimals must match across chains. Configure steps for custom:[Configure a custom token](https://developers.circle.com/cctp/expanded-assets/quickstarts/configure-custom-token) .


### Native on Arc Testnet, end to end


To work the end-to-end flow, you need a deployer address you will reuse on every supported blockchain you want coverage on and Arc Testnet[USDC for gas](https://www.arc.io/blog/sponsored-transactions-on-arc-with-usdc-as-gas) and Iris fees. Pick your token name, symbol, decimals, and a salt; those inputs, and the deployer address will define a single` tokenId` . Each chain still gets its own token contract and balances; CCTP routes against the shared id.


Call` deployCrossChainToken` on Arc’s` CrossChainTokenService` . The` CREATE3` service deploys the token and its per-token manager. Transfer limits should be set in the deploy params so the managers are not left at zero (zero blocks transfers).


You can read the` tokenId` from the deploy receipt, then quote Iris and call` deployRemoteCrossChainToken` from Arc so the same identity appears on the second chain. Make use of[Circle's forwarding service](https://www.circle.com/blog/introducing-our-new-crosschain-forwarding-service-now-integrated-into-cctp) by including` FORWARD` in the quote if you want Circle to complete delivery without destination gas. Check the live fee before you send as quotes differ by pair.


Once the token contracts are deployed, you will want to mint supply on Arc. To run a crosschain transfer, approve the per-token manager, quote a transfer (again with` FORWARD` if you want), and call` crossChainTransfer` . When the destination balance updates, you can be sure the route works.


Addresses, ABI quirks, and exact parameters live in the[crosschain ERC-20 deployment quickstart](https://developers.circle.com/cctp/expanded-assets/quickstarts/deploy-native-crosschain-token) . Confirm the Arc Testnet service address on the[contract addresses](https://developers.circle.com/cctp/expanded-assets/references/contract-addresses) page before you ship.


## What's next: Move from Arc testnet to production


With the route live, applications built on Arc can settle payments, post collateral, and[show balances on Arc](https://www.arc.io/blog/supporting-arc-in-wallets-one-balance-usdc-fees-and-complete-history) , and move the same economic asset to another supported EVM chain when rebalancing or a venue there needs it, under one bridge identity.


Wire those flows into your application, extend the identity to any other domain you need (re-quote Iris each time), and tighten caps and roles before mainnet. Configuring an existing ERC-20 instead of native? Start with the[custom token quickstart](https://developers.circle.com/cctp/expanded-assets/quickstarts/configure-custom-token) . Also check out the developer documentation for all the details about CCTP for non-USDC assets.
